claims.text: Compositional modification can tune the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic HEAs in low-dimensional applications.
Substitutional alloying with varying concentrations of Fe, Co, Ni, Ti, V, and Cr is a suitable compositional-tuning method.
Fe, Co, and Ni are magnetic alloying elements in the proposed HEA system.
Ti, V, and Cr are non-magnetic alloying elements in the proposed HEA system.
Arc melting followed by annealing at 1000°C for 24 hours will ensure alloy homogeneity.
Annealing at 1000°C for 24 hours will stabilize the microstructure.
Compositional modification changes the crystal structure of the HEA.
Compositional modification changes the lattice parameter of the HEA.
Composition-induced structural changes modify magnetic exchange interactions.
Composition-induced structural changes modify magnetic anisotropy.
Modified exchange interactions and magnetic anisotropy change magnetization behavior.
Changes in magnetization behavior alter the magnetocaloric effect.
The proposed compositional modification will produce a 20% increase in isothermal entropy change relative to the baseline at a magnetic-field change of 2 T.
The isothermal entropy change can be determined from SQUID magnetometry measurements.
Restricting compositional variation to ±10 at.% from the baseline will maintain the low-dimensional structure.
Restricting compositional variation to ±10 at.% from the baseline will avoid phase separation.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 20% increase in ΔS, but the falsification rule allows the hypothesis to survive when at least 75% of samples show increases only slightly above 10%. Thus, the test does not decisively evaluate the stated 20% prediction.
